member.name: FindGapsBeneathUnverified
member.para: The six chapters the write-off cost. "Ovaron" (Perry Rhodan Silber-Edition 48, 16:38:37, build 411, run 2026-08-26; investigated 2026-08-28). Chapter 14 sits at 7:15:21.68 and chapter 21 at 10:19:08.62, and chapters 15-20 fill the three hours between them. Every one of the six is announced - confirmed against the user's Google Play Books copy of the same book, whose chapter lengths from 14 on (38:40, 23:32, 19:32, 25:15, 18:30, 29:49, 28:19) chain to within 10 s of where the run itself put chapter 21, and then by reading each position with ggml-large-v3-turbo, which hears all six cleanly.

What went wrong. Those six breaks carry no jingle - all 34 of the book's jingles lie outside the span - so the jingle-first pass could not reach them, and the silence pass read all 40 of the gap's pauses of 1.5 s and over with ggml-small and came back with nothing. The recognizer had swallowed each announcement while writing a confident transcript of the narration behind it: the run's own window probe 29.9s@7:53:53.21 opens 0.0-11.2 (p=0.71) "Auf den Bildschirm stand Leftrans duesteres Gesicht." - eleven seconds of segment carrying one short sentence, with "Kapitel 15. Bericht Ovaron." (2.5 s of clear speech, 1.75 s into the window) simply absent. Reproduced byte-for-byte offline with the same model and framing, so it is neither machine nor thread-count dependent. It is the same failure SweepSubFloorSilencesAsync already records ("Whisper's long-form decode swallowed the announcement ... while any short window aimed at the same audio read them cleanly").

None of the three re-reads in RegionProber can fire on that shape: two want a window that came back empty, the third a window that heard the number but not the word. Ovaron's windows came back full of plausible narration with neither - indistinguishable from the overwhelmingly common case of a pause that is not a chapter break at all.

Why the re-probe never got its turn. The empty 14-21 stretch left a six-chapter jump, which tripped the implausible-hole rule against a chapter 21 that was perfectly correct. Two re-reads confirmed "Kapitel 21", so the mark was kept and the number written off - and FindGaps then refused to pair 14 with 21 at all, which took the stretch away from the one pass that would have read it. The same run's re-probe ran for chapter 23 (10:45:30.75-11:29:18.00) and chapter 30 (12:55:07.11-13:52:22.03) and recovered both.

What it costs to let the re-probe look. Measured from that run's own log: 31 s for the 44 min gap and 59 s for the 57 min one, so on the order of three minutes for Ovaron's three-hour stretch. The re-probe reads candidate pauses, not the whole region, which is what makes looking affordable where Scan transcribing the stretch would not be.

The residual lead the first investigation dismissed. That investigation recorded 9:50:34 as the only place in three hours where Whisper began a segment with a number - "20 Tarakan hatte das Tal jetzt zum vierten Mal ueberflogen" - and let it go. It was chapter 20, with the word swallowed exactly as above. A bare number surfacing where the chapter word went missing is evidence, not noise.

member.name: Normalize
member.para: What a greedy left-to-right scan cost. On "Die Cyber-Brutzellen" (2026-08-01) chapter 14's announcement at 7:01:30 was read as 40, and chapters 15 through 29 - every one of them detected, refined and correctly placed - then failed "greater than 40" one after another and were discarded: a 17 h audiobook came out marked as far as 6:21 and no further.

What "the earliest survives" costs when something plants a phantom first. "Atlan" (build 392, 2026-08-24): a hallucinated second match on chapter 5's announcement was marked as chapter 6 at 2:28:25.26, and when Re-probe later placed the real chapter 6 at 2:47:23.42 the filter had two marks numbered 6 to choose between and kept the earlier one - the phantom. The tie-break is not the defect (it is what keeps an in-text mention from displacing a real chapter, and nothing in this filter can tell the two apart), which is why the fix was to settle the collision before the filter ever sees it rather than to change how it resolves ties.
